correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge2\), transitivity of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)\) gives \(\mathbb E X=1\); any two distinct nonzero idempotents are independent, and only pairs with dependent squared-coordinate vectors are inadmissible. For odd \(q\), counting squares and signs by support gives \(B=\frac{q-1}{2}((2q-1)^n-2q^n+1)\), proving \(\operatorname{Var}X=1-B/((q^n-1)(q^n-q))\); for even \(q\), the variance equals one. In characteristic two, independence over \(\mathbb F_2\) among fixed vectors forces independence over \(\mathbb F_q\), yielding the full law by Gaussian inversion. All dimension, field and normalization boundaries have been checked, and ten complete matrix-ensemble scans independently matched. The proof does not extrapolate infinite claims from tests.

originality.rationale: The original claim is the exact finite-q, all-dimension odd-characteristic variance correction and unified characteristic bifurcation. The complex existence theorem (arXiv:2512.12418), special singular 3D result (arXiv:2609.25023), finite-field perfect-algebra isomorphism census (arXiv:2310.12368), later mean-one observation and conjectural asymptotic survey (arXiv:2610.22248), and accessible indexed related results do not imply this second moment. Shintani descent is acknowledged as broader coverage for the even-characteristic corollary, not claimed new as an abstract semilinear theorem. Residual unindexed-equivalence risk remains.

value.rationale: Uniform labelled perfect evolution algebras form the full \(\mathrm{GL}_n\)-matrix ensemble motivating recent idempotent-count questions. The exact second moment refines a known mean-one identity, distinguishes odd from even characteristic for every \(n\ge2\), and supplies a strict finite-field deviation with an explicit support-collision explanation; the even-characteristic full law resolves an entire natural distribution. This is a family-wide structural statistic, not a small arbitrary slice or a known table recomputation. No downstream theorem is claimed.
